summary: Commercial Type's specimen disguised as a one-off food magazine: the home page is the issue's table of contents, six commissioned articles (interview, essay, fiction, recipe, news, listicle) that each open as a subpage. An editor's note explains the idea. A sticky header button randomizes the type pairing across the whole page, and the colophon names whichever families are currently in use, with catalogue links.

instances.variantDefinition: A slim bar fixed to the top of the viewport for the whole page: name, foundry link and a buy/get button, sometimes site toggles (invert colours)
instances.look: Sticky white 80px header: small blue 'Commercial' logo left, two tiny icon buttons right (● theme toggle, ↻ 'Randomize type pairing')
Two 19px icon buttons in the sticky header: a filled dot (theme toggle) and a circular arrow (randomize type pairing)
instances.ux: The ↻ button picks a new display/text family pairing from Commercial Type's catalogue (Feature, Action Condensed, Frame, Algebra, Review…) and re-sets the whole issue in it, rotating the icon each time; the dot flips light/dark. Per the editor's note, the article subpages add leading and point-size controls
instances.learn: One 'shuffle the pairing' button turns a static magazine into a pairing explorer: every click shows the same real content in another headline/text combination

reconstruction.layout: Icons ~19×16px, 16px apart, right-aligned in the 80px sticky header
reconstruction.behaviour: Click → random pairing applied to headline (display), deck and text roles site-wide; CSS --rotation increments to spin the icon; theme toggle swaps to a dark theme; colophon family names re-resolve to the active pairing

instances.look: Centred nameplate 'The Food Issue' in a black-outlined box (SVG, ~214×45px) on white, standing in for a hero above the contents

Six article teasers zig-zagging left and right down a white page, each a small caps section label (INTERVIEW, ESSAY, FICTION, COOKING, NEWS, EATING), a big black serif headline ('Helen Rosner on the Banal and the Beautiful', 'Becoming a Regular', 'A Beginner's Guide to Kuih'…), an italic dek and a byline
instances.feel: Serious, generous, like a real magazine cover list
instances.ux: Each teaser is a link card to the full article subpage; there is no image, so the type carries the page
instances.learn: Commission real writing in several genres and present it as a contents page: the hierarchy of label, headline, dek and byline is the specimen, and people actually read it

reconstruction.layout: Container ~1320px; cards 749px wide alternating x=60 and x=631 (overlapping centre column), ~80px vertical gaps; card heights 240–416px depending on headline lines
reconstruction.typography: Label ~13px Feature Text Bold caps; headline ~80px Feature Display (Bold), leading ~1.0, tight tracking, sentence case with non-breaking spaces to control breaks; dek ~24px Feature Deck Italic; byline ~24px Feature Text Regular
reconstruction.behaviour: Static; whole card is an anchor; small black dots at card edges (likely the abstract illustrations, not rendered in capture); fonts swap with the pairing randomizer
reconstruction.content: Six real, commissioned pieces about food and New York: interview (Navneet Alang), essay (Helena Fitzgerald), fiction (Robin Sloan), cooking (Diane Chang), news (Daniel Pravit Fethke), listicle (Christian Schwartz with Veronica Gan and Barnny Lim)
reconstruction.assets: Abstract illustrations by Derrick Schultz and Di-Andre Caprice Davis (on the article pages)
